moves: Brew thermostat: unplug Ba and Bb and join them with J. The thermocouple goes in the thermostat's place.
Steam thermostat: unplug Sa and Sb and plug them onto wires Sa and Sb from the SSR. The thermostat can stay, disconnected, or come out.
Pump: unplug Pb and plug it onto wire 3. Wire P goes on the terminal Pb came off, and N piggybacks on Pa.
Brew switch: unplug B4 from spade 4 and plug it onto L. Spade 4 stays empty.
Steam switch: move S4 from spade 4 to spade 1. Unplug S5 and park it: it stays live, so insulate its end and tie it down.
Lamps: the steam lamp now sits across the SSR, so it lights when the boiler isn't heating. The brew lamp goes dark for good, and the power lamp works as before.

Evo Pro and E24: on most, each switch's connectors sit together in one combined block. Take each connector out, insulate it on its own and label it before you start, because some stay in the machine unplugged. The official parts list adds self-fusing silicone tape for this.
keep: Power switch and power lamp: unchanged.
Pump thermal fuse (110 °C) and boiler thermal fuse (184 °C): unchanged.
Steam switch spades 2 and 3 still carry mains as they did stock, and spade 1 now does too, because S4 moves there.
Brew switch spade 5 stays on the valve's feed, which the PCB now drives, so empty spade 4 is live too whenever brew is on and the valve is open. Keep it clear of everything.
Low-voltage wires go only on brew spades 1 and 2, which were empty, and steam spades 4 and 5, which this install frees.
As drawn, the SSR sits on the elements' neutral side, so the elements stay connected to line whenever the machine is on, heating or not.
Valve, heating elements and earth wires: unchanged.

Screen IO28 on the Gen 3.5, IO17 on the Gen 3, TX on the headless board

shelly.name: Shelly smart relay
shelly.src: fusio's Classic Pro + Shelly Plus 1PM drawing (Gaggiuino Discord, unofficial, drawn on the May 2024 custom wiring), adapted by this site to the Plug-and-Play harness, with the machine's neutral kept off the Shelly's terminals

ends: Nylon flag female 6.3 mm, blue: two wires (with SH1)
Nylon flag female 6.3 mm, red: one wire
L1a-L1b.note: Line from the socket to the power switch's input. With the Shelly it only carries the switch's signal to the Shelly, through SH4. At the socket it shares a blue two-wire flag with SH1: on a kit harness, cut L1a's red flag off and crimp both wires into a blue one. If the socket moves out into the Shelly's enclosure, it needs to be that much longer: extend it with a BN1.25 butt splice under silicone heat shrink, or cut a new one.

L4a-L4b.frm: BN2 S6 Shelly output splice (right side)
ends: BN2 butt splice under silicone heat shrink
Nylon female 6.3 mm: X1b plugs in
L4a-L4b.note: With the Shelly, the L4a flag comes off the power switch: cut it off by the switch and join its two wires to SH3 in splice S6. The lamps then light whenever the Shelly has the machine on.

L4a-L4c.frm: BN2 S6 Shelly output splice (right side)
ends: BN2 butt splice under silicone heat shrink
SSR spade (fork) for two wires (with L4d-L4c)
L4a-L4c.note: Switched line into the SSR, now from the Shelly's output through splice S6, which sits by the power switch where L4a was, so the length holds.

N1a-N1c.note: Neutral from the socket to the pump fuse and on to the PCB. N1c's flag now plugs onto the tab of SH2's piggyback, on the socket's N tab. If the socket moves out into the Shelly's enclosure, it needs to be that much longer: extend it with a BN1.25 butt splice under silicone heat shrink, or cut a new one.

BN2-N1c.note: Shares the N1c flag with N1a-N1c, which now plugs onto SH2's piggyback. If the socket moves out into the Shelly's enclosure, it needs to be that much longer: extend it with a BN1.25 butt splice under silicone heat shrink, or cut a new one.

G1a-G1b.note: Earth from the socket to the chassis. If the socket moves out into the Shelly's enclosure, it needs to be that much longer: extend it with a BN1.25 butt splice under silicone heat shrink, or cut a new one.

ends: Nylon flag female 6.3 mm, blue: two wires (with L1a-L1b)
Bootlace ferrule in the Shelly's L terminal
add.note: The Shelly's supply, and the line its relay switches. It shares the socket's L tab with L1a-L1b, in one blue flag. Short when the Shelly sits beside the socket.

add.to: BN2 S6 Shelly output splice (left side)
ends: Bootlace ferrule in the Shelly's O terminal
BN2 butt splice under silicone heat shrink
add.note: The Shelly's switched output, run to splice S6 by the power switch, where L4a's two wires now start. Everything after it is off while the Shelly is off.

ends: Nylon female 6.3 mm
Bootlace ferrule in the Shelly's SW terminal
add.note: Takes L4a's place on spade 4 and tells the Shelly the power switch is on. It carries mains from L1a-L1b through the switch, so treat it as a mains wire.

ends: Piggyback spade 6.3 mm on the socket's N tab
Bootlace ferrule in the Shelly's N terminal
add.note: Powers the Shelly itself. The N1c flag plugs onto the piggyback's tab, so the machine's neutral never runs through the Shelly: Shelly's own docs warn that using its terminals as a bridge for load current can overheat it.
